Contract: the declared-absence read (WI-308): check_doc_refs reads an optional `<path> — <reason>` file (--declared-absences, default docs/declared-absences) and reclassifies a reference to any listed path as UNTRACED with the DECLARED reason quoted back, rather than dangling. The seam exists because a second reader needs the same facts: tests/test_dogfood_sync.py loads the file as its SCAFFOLD_OMISSIONS declaration, so the file — not an import — is the shared home, keeping the stdlib-only kit script free of any dependency on a test module. Fail-soft in the safe direction: an absent file, or a line carrying no separator, declares nothing and leaves the path dangling, so a malformed entry can never silence real rot.

the owner decision registry read (WI-322, OI-10 ruled option (b)): gen_open_items loads one row per decision (OI-ID/Title/Status/OneLine/Decision/BlastRadius/Options/Recommendation/WI-Refs) and renders every Status=pending row as a brief card. A ruled row is history, not a decision, and is deliberately NOT rendered - the Decisions log in docs/log.md is its record. -000 example rows are dropped, the copy-ready placeholder convention every other registry uses; an absent registry renders an empty queue rather than failing, so a repo carrying no decisions still has a surface.

the generated owner surface (WI-322): the ONLY document a human reads for pending decisions plus every Draft/Modified spine row's per-cell before/after. Contract of the emitted file: it carries an attestation-baseline stamp that --check re-reads (so a --since render is reproducible by the freshness gate), and a machine-local advisory region between explicit markers that --check MASKS before comparing (refs/llm/* facts do not transport with clone/push - the M-10/WI-266 rule inherited from the markdown block it replaces). The depth itself is computed by trace.reattest_model and the pending pointers by gen_trajectory.pending_block; this module renders, and if it ever disagrees with `trace.py --ratify` the brief is authoritative.

the attestation-model seam (WI-322): gen_open_items imports trace.reattest_model — the SINGLE computation of what a Draft/Modified spine row's chain looks like against its attested baseline (git archaeology + per-cell comparison) — and renders it as HTML, while trace.reattest_lines renders the same model as the markdown brief. Split out of reattest_lines rather than reimplemented, because a second copy of the baseline derivation in a second module is the paraphrase-not-decompose failure this kit exists to prevent; the markdown output was proven byte-identical across the extraction. A cross-component import (Generators -> Traceability core) declared here rather than retagged: the model belongs with the registries it reads, and the renderer belongs with the generators.

trace_text.py module: the spine-row TEXT layer split out of trace.py (WI-329) - four PURE predicates (rows in, findings out, no I/O) plus the row primitives they share. provenance_findings(srs,llrs,tcs) and form_findings(srs,llrs,tcs) return gating findings that join trace's --strict exit_code; ac_advisories(srs) and paraphrase_advisories(srs,llrs) return warn-only advisories that never join a failure set; refs/is_example/is_draft are the shared row primitives, homed here as the lower layer so the dependency runs one way. Finding STRINGS are part of the contract: the three golden files assert them byte-for-byte, which is what makes the split provably behaviour-preserving.
Notes: source - trace_text consumes NOTHING by design: it is the pure predicate layer (rows in, findings out; no I/O, no git, no filesystem, no argv), which is what makes it testable in isolation and what the pure-core / I-O-shell split asks for. A Consumes seam here would mean the extraction failed to separate the concerns.
